judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the PIF TICK quality-mark badge (image text 'Trusted Information Creator / Patient Information Forum'), the only content of the third footer badge link, next to the Fundraising Regulator and Investing in Volunteers badge links. claimTrue: in the snapshot the img is all the link holds (link name 'Trusted Information Creator Logo', nameFrom contents, no title), and the alternative names the badge as a logo rather than stating a destination, so the sentence holds. captureDiffers: the live footer HTML fetched today is identical (same href, same img and alt) and the screenshot shows the badge row rendered normally; no difference touches the claim. elementFails: the href /prostate-information/further-help/our-award-winning-information redirects to 'Help review our award-winning information', whose section 'Our award-winning information' explains the PIF TICK, says it is awarded to 'trusted information creators', and shows this same logo. Read as link text in a row of accreditation badges, 'Trusted Information Creator' names the subject the link leads to (this accreditation), which by the rubric's R2 first test describes the purpose, so my lean is that it passes; the word 'Logo' describes the image but does not hide the subject. Against that, H30 asks the alternative to give the link's unique function, the landing page after the redirect opens with volunteer recruitment under a different title, and a user cannot tell it leads to the charity's own page rather than to the Patient Information Forum (as the two neighbouring badges lead to their accreditors). Competent auditors would reasonably disagree on whether a badge-name alternative suffices here, so the label is uncertain. Separately, the alternative omits 'Patient Information Forum' shown in the image, a text-equivalence point the claim does not raise.
